query: How does incident resolution efficiency vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Well-separated interpretable categories, but the query already names 'category' as a grouping axis and the original table has a 'category' column. This largely restates an existing focus/grouping dimension rather than opening a new relationship.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: External associational variable with clean, well-separated categories (printer, monitor, server, laptop...). One can segment resolution efficiency by asset type and compare meaningfully. Adds a genuinely new dimension beyond the query's stated axes.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated symptom categories that plausibly relate to how quickly incidents resolve. Grouping efficiency by symptom is an informative exploratory comparison, though 'malfunction_general' dominates (310/500), weakening some contrasts.

per_column.name: self_resolved_by_assignee
per_column.rationale: Clean binary split, but 'self resolved by assignee' is essentially a facet of the resolution process itself, closely tied to the efficiency focus rather than an external associational variable to compare against it.

per_column.name: software_trigger_present
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary segmentation that is external to the focus; efficiency can be compared for software-triggered vs not. Reasonable exploratory contrast, though the 54/446 imbalance limits the strength of comparison.

per_column.name: requires_replacement
per_column.rationale: Conceptually relevant (replacement likely lengthens resolution), but the near-constant distribution (14 true / 486 false) means the 'true' segment is too small for a meaningful, well-supported comparison.

judge.rationale: The set contains interpretable, well-separated categorical variables and several offer genuine external axes (affected_asset_type, failure_symptom_type, software_trigger_present) along which resolution efficiency can be segmented and compared. However, quality is diluted: incident_category largely restates an existing grouping axis, self_resolved_by_assignee is a facet of the resolution process rather than an independent associational variable, and requires_replacement is too near-constant (14/500) to support meaningful comparison. Several binaries are also heavily imbalanced, limiting contrast strength. Moderately informative for exploratory relationship discovery, but not strongly so.
